title: Fit a logistic regression with gradient descent and Newton's method
brief: Build the gradient X^T(p - y), the Hessian X^T D X + lambda I, a descent loop, a Newton loop, and an accuracy function, then compare how many passes each loop needs.
hints: The gradient is X.T @ (sigmoid(X @ w) - y) + ridge * w. No loop over examples is needed.
Let s = p * (1 - p) with p = sigmoid(X @ w). Then (X * s[:, None]).T @ X + ridge * np.eye(d) scales the rows of X without building a diagonal matrix.
In fit_gradient_descent, append the loss first, then compute the gradient, then break if np.linalg.norm(g) < tol, then update w = w - lr * g. That order makes history[0] the loss at zero weights.
newton_step returns delta = np.linalg.solve(hessian(...), gradient(...)). The caller subtracts it: w = w - delta. fit_newton follows the descent loop with that step.
Keep the small default ridge of 1e-8 in fit_newton. It keeps np.linalg.solve from failing when two columns are copies of each other.
train_accuracy compares the labels (predict_proba(w, X) >= 0.5) with y, and takes the mean.
